recs.name: Azure Memories
recs.tag: That is her own shade of blue.

lines.x: I'm sorry, we're not open yet. Please come back in the afternoon.
Sorry about the timing. I'm not here to buy art; I just have some questions.
For your trouble.
(Slips a gold coin through the crack in the door)
This is...
Consider it a token of appreciation. And there's more where that came from, if you've got the information I need.
A pleasure to meet you in the flesh, sir.
Er, ahem... what can I help you with?
Last month, a painting that is very dear to me suffered moisture damage thanks to improper storage.
I've heard that a very skilled restoration painter lives here, so I thought I would try my luck.
Oh... that could be tricky. She's not easy to find.
Does she live outside town? I've got more gold coins.
(Takes out a gold coins from his sleeves)
No, she's in town, but she's a little eccentric. We keep our distance from her, when we can help it.
She's got a temper? Violent type? Or more of an arrogant artist?
Well... you might say she's got a sunny disposition.
Oh?

It's not so bad when she's at home painting, other than the strange noises, from time to time. When she's sketching outside, though... everyone stays as far away as they can. Don't want to get press ganged into modeling for her.
There's no getting away once she sets her eyes on you. You have to sit there and wait for her to finish, no matter what else you might have to do.
And, as you know, paintings aren't the quickest thing to get done... poof, there goes your whole day.
Why don't you just say no?
Yeah... why not just turn her down? Seems easy enough.
(Mutters to himself with a blank expression)
Sir? Are you okay?
I-I'm fine. I'm trying to think back to what she said to me, but I just can't remember a thing.
That's a little weird... heh.
Anyway, it doesn't matter. She's a little loopy, you know. Says lots of weird things.
Don't let the things she says get to you. I'm sure she doesn't mean any harm by them.
Heh... didn't think you'd turn around and start defending her.
She's a little off-kilter, sure, but she's never hurt anybody. Plus...
Half of what I sell here is her work. Her stuff is popular.
A hardworking painter! Now I'm even more curious.
Well, sir, if you insist, I can take you to her.
This is where she lives. I'll be on my way now.
You're not coming in with me?
Er... well, I have a thing.
Okay, then. Thanks.
(Takes out a few gold coins from his sleeves)
For your trouble.
Oh, thank you so much! That's kind of you. Please feel free to come by my shop if there's anything else I can help with.
Goodbye now.
Huh? Oh, alright, goodbye.
What a nice little hideout.
It is almost noon, and the sun shines brightly outside.

Inside, however, all the doors and windows are tightly shut, with only a few rays of sunlight leaking through the cracks between the boards that have been nailed to the windows, preventing the room from being entirely engulfed in darkness.
The visitor hears the faint sound of scratching coming from the darkest corner.
He straightens his robe and approaches a massive canvas standing upright. A woman is using her brush to fill it with color.

Should the brush be drier? But then the brush marks would be too distinct...
No, that's not the color that I wanted.
How's that? Does that look better?
The colors could run further down the canvas. I have to do it with a single stroke. No interruptions now... none whatsoever.
It's been a while...
Oh, it's you. Have a seat.
When was the last time you cleaned? You can't see anything in that mirror anymore.
Hah, are you belittling my humble abode, Father? You can't imagine the inspiration I find here.
You haven't changed a bit. You don't care about anything but your art.
You've changed a lot. Your brow didn't furrow like that.
Really...?
Something on your mind?
Well, if you don't want to talk about it, I won't pry.
The first time I saw you, you were absorbed in your painting, just like this.
The first time you saw me? When was that? It's been so long, I can't remember.
I was hiding behind that boulder, that day you met the Herald for the first time.
So you were by the water... all I remember is the beauty the Herald showed me. I've never seen a creature so beautiful.
The Herald must have felt your admiration, guiding you into we many after just one contact.
I've always been grateful.
But you turned around, one step from the ocean.
I'm not making excuses.
Did you abandon the many and turn against your kin just to finish this painting?
(Touches the canvas with a finger)
So beautiful, but burdened by so much sin.
I'm sorry.
But your regret hasn't stopped your brush.
You were too stubborn, too short-sighted. You trapped yourself in the canvas and failed to see the distant future.
You didn't understand the many. You couldn't fit in with the many. You should have nourished the many if you could not be assimilated.
That should have been your end. I am regretful, but joyful. We will become one, sister.
(Sleeves quiver)
Would you put that away for now? I want to finish this before it's all over.
(Straightens sleeves)
It took me a long time to get here. I can wait a little longer.
Good.
And there's something I wanted to ask you before I end your life.
Go on. My brush won't stop, though.
Why did you choose to leave us?
Life is eternal in we many. We are inextricably linked, sharing our joy, anger, sorrow, happiness.
That 'sharing' you're talking about is just about robbing me of all emotion, transforming me into a mouth for the will of the many.
Your outbursts are meaningless. It will not soothe your anger, nor abate your sorrow. It will only make you wallow in boundless misery as you step ever closer to destruction.
We many have sealed away excess emotion. A constant state of heightened alertness is not conductive to the many's continued survival.
You should cast it away and embrace peace and tranquility with us, free from the trappings of your own emotion.
My cries of sorrow, anger and angst are the fertile soil of my art.
I never joined you to get peace or tranquility.
Then what did you want from us?
That's never changed, whether I chose to join or leave.
I want beauty, eternal beauty, dwelling in all life.
Didn't you find it?
A glimpse of the Herald's beauty was enough to change your life forever. Was that not enough?
The Herald left his seed in you, made you one of us, to partake in our beauty.
Yes, your bodies hold the ultimate beauty, beyond anything else.
But have you ever noticed it, appreciated it?
The choices you make guide you to eternal art, but you can't even be moved by art.
You faced survival and evolution, and your answer was to abandon the concept of beauty.
When I started to assimilate, I became numb. I couldn't create or appreciate.
You don't know how I felt when I realized that my brush was covered in dust... the pain I felt in that moment told me I had to leave the many.
So you could not let go of human desire.
Humanity created art as a form of self-expression. Humanity admires art to seek the ego within.
Humanity is looking into a mirror, as humanity always has.
It's selfish, and pathetic...
(Puts down the brush)
You've finished.
Yes, I have.
Blue. As far as the eye can see. You've seen the depths of the ocean, and you understand that the confines of the canvas are too small for the great waves.
You saw the sea... but what I painted was a puddle.
The destiny of water began in the ocean, and in the ocean it shall end.
That's the destiny of water, not the ocean.
You have put your last stroke on the canvas. It's time to go.
I spent months without sleep in order to finish it. You came at just the right time. Maybe you should take another look, as the first being to lay eyes on it.
To us, it's a piece of cloth with color on it. It has no meaning.
Cloth? No, you're wrong. You used to say that I couldn't see true greatness because I was fixated on the canvas. What about you, then?
What?
Every surface in the room begins to peel away, revealing an eerie hue of blue beneath.
The blue begins to devour other colors around it, as though alive.
It soon takes over the entire house, even the cracks between the planks on the window, blocking out the sun completely.
The room should have turned pitch-black, but instead it is blue as far as the eye can see.
An ominous blue, a sinister blue.
Ah... so this is the big picture. Literally.
I have far underestimated the progress that you've made in the past six months.
Go home, Father. You never saw me. You missed your chance to catch me.
What a shame...
You shouldn't have asked so many questions. Hunting and feeding don't need words.
You shouldn't have come looking for me on your own.
I see...
What is it?
Over the past few years, I have been troubled by my failure to reach the next stage of metamorphosis. I've been trying to find out why.
After thinking on it, I still have a human desire: curiosity. That's why I wasn't able to metamorphose any further.
Looks like you stopped at the same place. A part of the human is always there with you, and you can't put it down, no matter how much you want to.
Ah... what a shame.
Leave, Father. You won't become one of them, just like I couldn't. Run away, like I did.
*Hiss*—Not giving up?
You won't cut any deeper than a flesh wound.
...Damn.
What did you put on me?
Just a little mark.
You're far too powerful for me to purge on my own, but there will be kin who can. The mark will guide the way for them, and it will continue to beckon as long as you still draw breath.
I gave you a chance, Father.
You chose to run away. You should be prepared to run forever.
I've reached a dead end. There's no way forward for me. I shall remain on the path forever.
My carcass will nourish those who come after me, who will go further.
I respect your choice.
To the visitor's eyes, the blue around him begins to warp, struggling to break free.
Large lumps of slime fall to the ground and wriggle their way towards the visitor, crawling up his robes and leaving behind a wet trail.
They surround him tightly, the slime congealing into threads, then tentacles that bury him.
The last thing he sees as his vision fades away is the pitying gaze of a woman.
You think we're on the same path. But actually, our paths have only momentarily intersected.
You thought I ran away, but actually, I've just reached a crossroads.
The road keeps on going.
Goodbye.
Looks like I can't stay here anymore.
Where could I work undisturbed?
What was that sound?
You heard it too? I came to see what's going on.
Hey, is that a pile of rubble where the painter's house was?
Why would it collapse, all of a sudden?
I didn't see her outside today... she might be buried under all that.
Go get help!
Right.
Painter! Are you down there? Can you hear me?
What's going on? I came as soon as I heard. Why did the house collapse like that?
Where's the painter? And that visitor who wanted his painting restored?
If you've got time to ask questions, you've got time to dig!
I brought help!
Did you see anything?
No. What about you?
(Shake heads in unison)
Nothing, not even a body.
Did they leave?
We went around the town on our way here. No one saw the painter.
Hey, what's this?
A painting?
It's totally unharmed after being buried under rubble for so long?
What's the painting of? I can't tell.
All we can see is a corner, and it's all blue. Is it the sky? Or the...
Shh...
We'll know once we dig it out.
Whoa—!
What is it?
What the heck is this?!
A ball of slime clings to his palm, shimmering under the sun, and leaving sticky threads as he tries to pull his hand free of the canvas.

recs.name: Blue Notes
recs.tag: Follow, follow, follow the river, until the stream's end.

lines.x: Tick, tock...
Brush, draw...
Tick, tock...
Hello! You've got a package!
Please leave it at the door, thank you.
No problem!
And now I've forgotten what I was going to draw...
*Sigh*...
Never mind. I'll think about it later.
I should see what's in this package.
A painting?
But I make paintings, not buy them. Who is it from?
Strange. There's no sender or recipient.
Deepcolor knows, however, that it is meant for her.
Everything about it is familiar, from the colors to the texture.
Thank you, whoever sent it.
She leaves it by the easel, and resumes her painting.
She eventually finishes her latest work, but it is not the image she had envisioned. It is a reproduction of the 'painting.'
She finds her attention constantly drawn to that curious sense of familiarity, her eyes wandering from the canvas, her mind recreating the colors in its frame...
Maybe it's time for a break.
So many visitors today...
And what do you want?
To watch you draw. Any new paintings today?
Not yet.
But there's something on the canvas.
A stream, a forest, a wooden hut?
It's a reproduction. Someone sent me a painting, and it was all I could think of, so I just copied it.
Copying is painting too.
The ideas and techniques aren't mine. It's just practice; the painting doesn't belong to me.
That doesn't make a difference to me. I like it, as long as it's information that you painted with your own hand using your own brush and paint.
Anyway, I'm not painting today. Go.
What is it? You're entranced by the painting too?
It feels... familiar.
Don't you think so?
Yes, that sense of familiarity is what's preventing me from moving my brush. You can take it if you want.
But you've already seen it. Would me taking it change anything?
I suppose not...
What do we do, then?
Investigate? Explore?
No choice, I suppose... as you say.
Let's go!
Hey, are you not going to prepare at all? At least bring the painting?
You want to know where that package is from?
Yes. There's no sender or recipient, but it was clearly meant for me, so I wanted to know where it came from.
It couldn't have just—
I'm sorry, but I don't remember handling this one at all.
Huh?
It wasn't there when I went through the checkpoint when I came in. Are you sure I delivered it?
Don't worry though, I'll look it up. Might be some kind of anti-scam exercise from HR.
Give me a moment.
Where did you go?
The Messenger who delivered it says he doesn't remember...
I asked my friends. They know where it came from.
Where?
Follow the river and keep going. You'll see it.
A stream, a forest, a wooden hut.
You must be joking. How many streams are there in Terra?
My friends gave me the location. I'll lead the way.
Alright, wait here...
Where are you going?
Fetching my brush and canvas.
Wait! One moment.
What is it?
Let me catch my breath...
Alright.
How long have we been walking?
Days? Weeks?
Are you tired? Do you need me to carry your tools for you?
No, I'm a painter. I can carry my own gear...
Are you thinking about picking up painting?
I'd love to, but I couldn't learn it even if I tried.
Then help me get my paints ready. If we're taking a break, I want to use that time to paint something.
Alright.
Still no good...
Even facing completely different scenery, Deepcolor still ends up drawing the scene from the painting.
What's wrong with the one you're painting now?
I haven't drawn the hut yet, but... it's strange.
Why is it exactly the same, even when I'm using different paints?
Are you still copying?
Yeah...
Is it really copying if you're drawing natural scenery like it's real?
That's called imitation.
Is that different?
Yeah.
Then shouldn't you be calling it imitation, rather than copying?
Stop confusing the concepts...
Look in front of you.
On the other side of the canvas, Deepcolor finds herself looking at the scenery she had just depicted.
What's going on? I thought it was a meadow in front of us. Where did the stream come from?
You draw well. It's exactly like nature.
Do we follow this stream to our destination?
Perhaps...
This is getting stranger by the moment...
Can you help me put away the easel, assistant?
Alright.
What are you doubting, Deepcolor?
This feels... familiar...
That painting again?
It's this place. The forest and the stream.
This is the place the painting depicts...
I see the wooden hut. The one in the painting.
We're here...
Is this the place?
It looks the same from where I am.
Let's go in, then.
I'll wait for you at the door.
You're not coming?
I can't. I don't see the door.
Here's the door. Look, I opened it.
I'm sorry, I still don't see anything.
You go. I'll wait here.
Wait for me, then. I'll be back soon.
No one has lived here for a long time. The furniture is battered and broken, paintings are scattered everywhere, and there is a thick layer of dust on everything.
She feels an intense familiarity. Not in an eerie sense like that painting, but one full of intimacy and yearning.
It's like...
Home?
Deepcolor picks up a painting and brushes away the dust, revealing the tattered truth.
When painting becomes life, life becomes poison.
There is no choice but to follow it downstream.
Trees, stream, hut... why are all the paintings the same?
Deepcolor takes a painting off the wall and blows away the past's shackles.
There is a paradise for painters in a faraway land...
Follow the stream, and you'll reach it.
*Cough* Isn't this an oval frame used for portraits? Why is it still the same?
Could the sketchbook be...
Deepcolor opens the sketchbook on the table. The pages flutter, revealing an aged warning.
The hand that cannot draw beauty, the heart that has never seen beauty. Heaven is out of reach, but self-destruction is near.
Follow the stream...
Every page is just the scenery outside.
Did the owner of this house go mad?
Well, she drew so many, so I might as well leave her this one.
The painting makes a dull sound as it hit the ground.
It will be forgotten here, to be buried in the dust.
Until...
Her last painting becomes eternity.
You're back. Did you find anything?
No.
What about the painting?
I left it inside. Didn't want to remember it anymore.
Can you paint now?
Here?
Yeah.
Won't I just end up drawing the same scenery again?
Only one way to find out.
I guess you're right. I'll try.
There.
Isn't it the same painting?
No. Look, the lighting and angle here, and the application of colors, all different.
Something's missing...
It's not a matter of technique... strange...
What is it?
...You said your friends told you the painting came from here.
Yes. Is there a problem?
Can your friends go inside the house?
No, they can't.
Then, how did they know where the painting came from?
'Follow the stream. It lies at the very end.'
That's what they said.
Oh?
What lies at the end of the stream?
What the owner of the house wanted.
Hm...
Put this painting away for me, assistant.
Alright.
Then, we can follow the stream.
What lies at the end of the stream?
Do you still have water, assistant?
Only the seawater before us.
I'm hungry... tired... nobody would come here to paint...
Paint? Of course not.
They come to survive.
Look.
The assistant points towards a pile of scattered painting tools.
The paint is all dried up, and broken easel pieces litter the floor.
Poor thing...
There is no place for her anywhere else.
Survival permits no impurity.
One must abandon everything else in order to survive.
Deepcolor sees a familiar picture frame amidst the reefs.
Broken, dying.
That's the painting from the package...
Yes.
She wanted to give it to me...
Yes.
And I left it behind in the house?
Yes. You don't need it anymore.
Perhaps I should... leave a souvenir?
We could send back the reproduction you made.
Let's do that.
What about us?
We keep going.
This is the end. Where are you going?
Deepcolor steps into the ocean.
The ocean took her, didn't it?
One who has touched seawater can never go back.
Did she have a choice?
No.
Then neither do I. Am I wrong?
Let's go, assistant. What was started must be finished.
It is not water that fills the oceans.
It is ink, paint, colors.
It seeps into every one of Deepcolor's nerve strands, wiping away all her emotions.
She becomes pure, perfect.
Many voices sing along with her, extolling the harmony of survival.
She ascends and tries to sing in harmony.
But she does not sing. She raises her brush.
The singing comes to an abrupt stop.
This is not how survival is expressed, Deepcolor.
I live. I must paint.
Painting does not protect. Painting does not nourish. It is illogical for survival.
Yes, but to paint is to live. How could I stop?
The brush dips into the ink of the ocean, and colors fly through the water.
Have you forgotten why you embraced the ocean?
Of course I haven't. Giving up painting for survival, and meeting the end in bitter hatred.
That's why she drowned. I'm alive. I must express.
I won't abandon color, canvas, or brush. I'm not stopping anymore.
Draw with me, assistant.
We must stockpile energy, overcome weakness, seek evolution.
Yes. We can paint even better.
In evolution, this is a fallacy.
So what?
I'm not heeding the call of the many. Whatever of me is left, I give to painting.
Stroke by stroke, she fills the sea with color.
Even the ocean could not stop her expression.
Seawater mixes with paint, separates, then mixes again, gradually leaving their mark on the ocean.
Come, assistant, this is a lot to do on my own.
Gather the colors to me. Don't let them disperse.
What did you say? Our brethren are gone?
It's their many. What has it to do with us, with me?
Is the palette ready? The ocean is waiting for us to color it!
Are you there, assistant?
Assistant?
Phew. I guess I'll stop there.
Blocks of blue form the subject of the painting on her canvas.
This is our story. But was the last part a little too intense?
The tentacles extending from the palette sway side to side, perhaps a sign of affirmation, or of denial.
The life of a Seaborn is so repressed, after all. Can't fault one for being a little radical in protesting it.
That's it for this painting. Let's cover it up and put it through the process, or HR really will kick me off the ship once more operators complain.
It was hard enough finding somewhere I can paint in peace, without having to deal with those things. I'd rather not be forced on the run again.
Hello! You've got a package!
Coming!
Operator Deepcolor? The stuff you ordered is here. Painting supplies and a picture frame.
Thank you.
Please check if everything is alright, then sign here.
Here?
Yes.
Yeah... hm.
I thought you'd write in blue too.
Ha.
Have a nice day!
Thank you!
Mm.
What should I paint next?
